title: Can Anarchism Work?
summary: Josh and Chuck give an overview of anarchism as a political philosophy: its core premise that humans are better off governing themselves without lasting institutions, the distinction from anarchy and from liberalism and communism, and varieties such as anarcho-syndicalism, mutualism, social vs. libertarian anarchism, and direct action. They trace history from Zeno and Taoism through the English Diggers, William Godwin, Proudhon ("property is theft"), Bakunin and the violent propaganda-of-the-deed era (McKinley assassination, Haymarket, Sacco and Vanzetti), the Spanish anarchist villages, the 1960s counterculture and The Anarchist Cookbook, Occupy Wall Street, Christiania in Denmark, Chiapas, and Somalia. The episode closes with listener mail about suicide-reporting language and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and tour dates
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck mention upcoming live shows in Salt Lake City, Phoenix and Melbourne, note Jerry is out, and introduce the topic of anarchism.

segments.title: What anarchism is and is not
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish anarchism from anarchy and chaos, describe the core premise that self-governance beats lasting institutions, and compare anarchism with liberalism and communism.

segments.title: Schools of anarchism and direct action
segments.summary: They survey varieties of anarchism including mutualism and anarcho-communism, anarcho-syndicalism and direct action versus petitioning the state, and feminism's rape crisis centers as an example.

segments.title: Social vs. libertarian anarchism and spontaneous order
segments.summary: Andreas Vetter's split between social and libertarian anarchism is discussed, along with Proudhon's idea of spontaneous order and examples of community organizations meeting needs.

segments.title: Ancient roots and debate on human nature
segments.summary: Early roots are traced to Lao Tzu, Indian holy men and Greek philosopher Zeno; the hosts debate whether people can govern themselves without police or courts and how a bad actor could affect a community.

segments.title: Diggers, Godwin and Proudhon
segments.summary: The English Diggers of the seventeenth century, Gerrard Winstanley's pamphlet, their suppression, William Godwin's writings, and Proudhon's 'property is theft' are covered.

segments.title: Bakunin, the First International and anarchist terrorism
segments.summary: Bakunin's split with Proudhon and Marx, the First International, and the violent propaganda-of-the-deed period that included assassinations of heads of state are described.

segments.title: Haymarket, McKinley, Homestead, Sacco and Vanzetti
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Haymarket affair, McKinley's assassination by Leon Czolgosz, the Homestead strike and Berkman's shooting of Frick, Emma Goldman, and the Sacco and Vanzetti case.

segments.title: Spain, counterculture, Anarchist Cookbook and Internet era
segments.summary: Anarchist villages in Spain and their defeat in the Spanish Civil War, the 1960s counterculture Diggers, The Anarchist Cookbook, and the Internet's role in spreading anarchist ideas are discussed.

segments.title: Modern examples: Occupy, Christiania, Somalia, Greece
segments.summary: Occupy Wall Street and Zuccotti Park, Christiania in Copenhagen, Somalia's collapsed government, and anarchist-run refugee shelters in Athens are presented as modern examples.

segments.title: Chiapas Zapatistas and closing remarks on anarchism
segments.summary: The hosts describe the self-sufficient anarchist villages in Chiapas tied to the Zapatistas, then close the anarchism discussion with a note that listeners should form their own opinions.

segments.title: Listener mail on suicide reporting language
segments.summary: A listener named Jared writes with recommended guidelines for discussing suicide: say died by suicide rather than committed suicide, avoid method and location details, and avoid speculating on causes. Josh and Chuck agree.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and email contact information and sign off.
